There are two statements and four conclusions I, II, III and IV are given below. Assuming the statements to be true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All the trains are scooters.

All the buses are scooters.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some scooters are train.

II. No train is a bus.

III. Some trains are buses.

IV. No scooter is a train.

options.text: Conclusion I and either conclusion III or IV follow.
Conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions I and IV follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7828457a2d0075cdfcc20c679a14187a0faf339f96fa26a29b281172cebf00da.png] 

I. Some scooters are train. → True (As, All the trains are scooters.)

II. No train is a bus. → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

III. Some trains are buses. → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

IV. No scooter is a train. → False (As, All the trains are scooters.)

Conclusion II and III forms a complementary pair.

Hence, conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

**A.** On Wednesday the gang was at its hideout in Jaitpur after stealing the phone.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The chef said, "You will like the potato chops I've cooked for you."

options.text: The chef said that I would like the potato chops she had cooked for me.
The chef said to me you will like the potato chops I've cooked for you.
The chef says you will like the potato chops I've cooked for you.
The chef said I will like the potato chops she had cooked for me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., The chef said that I would like the potato chops she had cooked for me.**

__
 
• **When converting a general statement to indirect speech, the main verb becomes 'said' or 'told' (if there's a listener).**
 
• Here, the main indirect verb would be '**said**', as there is no third person listener mentioned.
 
• The second person pronoun '**you**' becomes '**me**' in indirect speech__, as the speaker is supposed to directly refer to the reader.
 
• The __first person pronoun '**I**', however, becomes the third person pronoun '**He/she**'.__
 
• In reported speech, simple future tense verb **'__will like__**__' becomes the modal '**would like**'; while the present perfect '**have cooked**' becomes past perfect '**had cooked**__'.

**Thus, the indirect sentence is:***** **The chef said that** I would like** the potato chops **she had cooked** for **me**. *

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.**

Sneha, who is aspire to join the Indian army as a soldier, has cleared the physical fitness test.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., who is aspire.**

__
 
• Notice the way in which the pronoun '**who**' is used here.
 
• The subject of the sentence is the noun '**Sneha**' and the part 'aspire to join the Indian army as a soldier' is giving more information about this noun and is dependent on it.
 
• So, this part (between two commas) is actually an adjective clause__, as this group of words serves as an adjective for the noun '**Sneha**'.
 
• But;** a dependent clause (adjective, adverb clauses) does not have a verb.**
 
• __So, '**who is aspire**' is incorrect. Correct dependent clauses would be: '**who aspires**'.__
 
• Alternatively, '**who is aspire**' is wrong because, here, '**is**' becomes the main verb and would require a progressive form of the verb '**to aspire**', viz, '**who is aspiring**'.

**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***Sneha, **who aspires** to join the Indian army as a soldier, has cleared the physical fitness test.*
